title: Consultant Neurologist PAYE
description:
Our patients have often tried everything. Years of appointments, medications that did not work, conditions that slowly took over their lives. By the time they reach us, many have run out of road with conventional treatment. You could be the clinician that changes that.

We are Montu UK, one of the UK's largest medical cannabis clinics, and we are looking for Consultant Neurologists to join our clinical team.

About the role

You will assess and manage patients exploring cannabis based medicines, making the clinical call on whether treatment is appropriate and managing their care from there. This is still a young field. The evidence base is growing, best practice is being written in real time, and you will have a genuine hand in shaping it.

You do not need experience with cannabis based medicines. You need sound clinical judgement, an open mind and an interest in doing things differently. We provide full specialist training, and our multidisciplinary model means you are never working in isolation. Nurses and pharmacists handle pre consultation and follow up tasks, so your time is spent where it matters: with patients.

What you will be doing:

  • Providing high quality care for patients seeking medical cannabis treatment

  • Conducting patient consultations, including assessment and ongoing management

  • Contributing to clinical outcome data collection to support evidence based practice

  • Supporting clinical governance and maintaining robust standards of patient care

  • Working closely within a multidisciplinary team of nurses and pharmacists

  • Taking part in ongoing training and development, including bespoke specialist training in cannabis based medicines (CBPMs)

What you need:

  • Full GMC Registration

  • Completion of Specialist Training (CCST/CCT) or equivalent certification

  • On the GMC Specialist Register for Neurology

  • A genuine interest in alternative therapies

  • Willingness to participate in data collection and reporting

Why join us?

  • Highly competitive salary

  • Flexible working with full time or part time options

  • Comprehensive indemnity coverage. Montu covers all professional and clinical indemnity insurance for your work with us

  • Private healthcare scheme

  • No night shifts and no on call

  • CPD accredited medical cannabis education and specialist in house training from industry leaders

  • A collaborative multidisciplinary team of healthcare professionals

  • The chance to be part of a pioneering field and shape the future of medical cannabis care in the UK

Training and development:

  • Attendance at a recognised Medical Cannabis Course for Specialist Physicians, sponsored by Montu

  • Specialist training delivered by experts

  • Ongoing support on clinical protocols, prescribing practices and Montu's systems

Working arrangements:

  • Fully remote with flexible working hours and days

  • Standard sessions are 4 hours of patient consultations, and you choose your preferred days and hours

  • To support onboarding, we ask for a minimum commitment of 2 sessions per week (8 hours) initially, so you become confident with our platform

  • Appointments are 15 minutes for new and existing patients. Our multidisciplinary model means nurses and pharmacists handle pre consultation and follow up prescribing tasks, so Consultants focus on prescribing and patient care

About Montu

Montu UK is a leading digital health company specialising in cannabis based medicines. We exist to transform lives by improving access to safe, effective treatment and delivering an exceptional standard of care. We move quickly, we care deeply about our patients, and we are building something that did not exist in UK healthcare five years ago.

If that sounds like your kind of place, we would love to hear from you.

title: Solutions Engineer - UK (German Speaking)
description:
😎 Our Culture

Quantum Metric's number one objective is happy people, diverse and inclusive culture. We’re passionate about empowering our people to become the best version of themselves, offering coaching and training programs designed to accelerate their career in whatever direction they choose.

As a remote-first company, we understand the importance of building an engaged, diverse, and fun place to work. We hold regular company-wide events, seasonal challenges, and Quantum Metric sponsored local outings when Zoom becomes too much. We also have a number of Employee Resource Groups that provide spaces to discuss, share, and reflect on topics that impact us both inside and outside of work - from being new to SaaS or navigating it as a first-time parent, to overcoming the barriers faced as Black, Hispanic, Asian American and Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander, LGBTQIA or other underrepresented backgrounds.

We are also passionate about the connections we build with our customers. You’ll not only work with some of the world’s most recognized brands, but build lasting relationships.

At Quantum Metric we value all types of experience and education and don’t expect you to meet every qualification for this position. We are most interested in the unique perspective you can bring and your ability to uphold our values of passion, persistence, and integrity.

🚀About the Role

As an Enterprise Solutions Engineer (EMEA) at Quantum Metric, you will serve as a trusted technical advisor supporting complex, high-value sales opportunities across the region. Working in close partnership with Enterprise Account Executives, you will engage with large, multinational organizations to help them transform how they understand and optimize digital customer experiences.

In this role, you will guide the technical strategy for enterprise deals, aligning Quantum Metric’s platform with strategic business initiatives. title: Senior Sales Recruiter
description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the Role:

Let’s be honest: 2026 is a strange time to be in Talent Acquisition. Most recruiters are currently looking at their own internal dashboards with a sense of unease. They’re seeing the pivots, the shrinking req loads, and the ‘doing more with less’ memos. If you’re currently at a startup that’s struggling to find its footing, or a business where the hiring bar has dropped just to fill seats, you know exactly how fragile that ‘growth’ story feels.

Samsara is the exception. We are a fortress in a volatile market. We are a $2B ARR, NYSE-listed powerhouse that sells essential technology to the physical operations powering the global economy.

And we aren't just stable—we’re expanding. Our UK Mid-Market team grew 70% year-over-year last year, and we need the talent engine to match that velocity. We aren't looking for someone to manage inbounds; we’re looking for a recruiter who wants to move from a shaky seat into a high-conviction, high-growth environment where the fundamentals actually make sense.

The Challenge:

  • Self-Sourced: You own your destiny. You will be expected to find, engage, and convert your own pipeline using best-in-class tools like HireEZ, Juicebox, and LinkedIn Recruiter.
  • The High Talent Bar: We aren't looking for CV pushers. You will be expected to act as a rigorous gatekeeper, ensuring that only the top 1% of gritty, A player sales hunters make it into our process.
  • Technical Assessment: You aren't checking vibes. You will be conducting deep-dive sales assessments, evaluating discovery mechanics, and ensuring every candidate has a structured methodology for success.

In this role, you will:

  • Execute & Deliver: Your mission is to fuel the Sales Account Executive engine. You will deliver high-quality, targeted pipelines at pace across EMEA, including the UK, France, Germany, and the Netherlands.
  • Own the Data: You are the CEO of your funnel. You will have total ownership of your response rates, passthrough rates, and talent market mapping. We make decisions based on data, not gut feel.
  • Partner with Sales Heavyweights: Work directly with our Sales VP and GTM leaders to align on hiring strategies that move the needle. You are a consultant, not an order-taker.
  • Master the Craft of Strategic Talent Acquisition: We hire for execution but develop for mastery. You will be mentored by some of the most sophisticated talent leaders in SaaS, learning how to move beyond execution to becoming a strategic talent partner who can influence the trajectory of an entire region.

Strong Backgrounds successful in this role:

  • The Agency Foundation: You started your career in a fast-paced recruiting agency. You still have that hunter DNA and the resilience to handle a relentless quarterly pace.
  • In-House Impact: In-house SaaS sales recruiting experience within a high-talent bar GTM organisation. You've proven you can translate agency grit into internal success.
  • EMEA Experience: You’ve successfully closed reqs in the UK and at least one other European market.
  • Technical Acumen: You can speak the language of sales. You know the difference between an order-taker and a territory owner. You have experience hiring for a scaling playbook environment and understand how to identify the elite within this market from the B players.

The Ideal Candidate is:

  • Foundational Mastery: The goal is to bridge the gap between execution and influence. You are here to build the bulletproof foundations of an exceptional recruiter—learning how to own a region, influence high-level stakeholders, and use data as a weapon.
  • Focused & Structured: You understand that structuring your inputs—sourcing volume, message personalization, and rigorous screening—is the only way to get consistent output.
  • Data-Minded: You study your own conversion rates and market talent availability to stay ahead of hiring needs.
  • Continuous Process Iteration: You possess a relentless drive for self-improvement. You iterate on your outreach and your screening questions based on what the data tells you.

What’s in it for you?

  • Build the Foundation for Leadership: We believe leadership is a set of skills, not just a job title. In this role, you will develop the data literacy to lead a boardroom with metrics, the strategic insight to advise VPs on market conditions, and the technical acumen to assess elite GTM talent.
  • Elite Exposure: You will be exposed to a broad range of international roles and learn from some of the best sales and recruiting leaders in the industry.
  • The Fortress Stability: NYSE-listed, GAAP profitable, and essential to the global economy. We are building for the long term, which means your career development here is backed by real revenue, not just a VC’s hopes.

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email accessibleinterviewing@samsara.com or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here.

description:
Headquarters: Franklin Parish, Louisiana, United States

 URL: http://www.mitratech.com

 At Mitratech, we are a team of innovators focused on building world-class products that simplify operations in the Legal, Risk, Compliance, and HR functions. We are a close-knit, globally dispersed team that thrives in an ecosystem that supports individual excellence and takes pride in a diverse, inclusive culture centered on great people practices, learning opportunities, and fun! Our culture blends entrepreneurial spirit with enterprise investment, giving you the chance to move quickly with some of the most complex, leading-edge technologies available.

 For over 35 years, the experts at Mitratech have been focused on solving the complex needs. Today, we serve 20,000 client companies of all sizes globally, representing 30% of the Fortune 500 and over 500,000 users in over 160 countries.

 As we continue to grow, we’re always looking for resourceful, enthusiastic, and fresh perspectives. Join our global team and see what makes Mitratech a truly exceptional place to work!

 This role is based in the US and operates as a key member of a globally distributed marketing team, collaborating closely with colleagues across the US, CAD, UK, and EMEA to deliver consistent, high-performing digital programs at scale.

 Job Overview

 The Associate Product Marketing Manager, GRC will support the go-to-market strategy and execution for select products in Mitratech's GRC portfolio. This role will focus on positioning and messaging, competitive intelligence, product launches, and sales enablement, working closely with Product Marketing, Product Management, Sales, Demand Generation, and Customer Marketing. We're looking for a hands-on marketer who can own defined projects, turn complex product and market information into clear, customer-facing messaging, and collaborate effectively across teams. The ideal candidate is curious, proactive, organized, and comfortable using data and AI tools to make marketing work more efficient.

 Essential Duties & Responsibilities

 Launch & GTM Execution

• Support go-to-market activities for new products, capabilities, and feature releases.

• Translate product updates into launch messaging, sales materials, presentations, and other customer-facing assets.

• Coordinate with Product Management, Demand Generation, Customer Marketing, and Sales to support launch execution.

• Support cross-sell and upsell initiatives by developing messaging and materials that help customers understand the value of additional products and capabilities.

• Help ensure product positioning is consistently represented across relevant marketing and sales channels.

 Sales Enablement

• Develop and maintain sales enablement materials including buyer's guides, competitive guides, presentations, FAQs, objection-handling resources, and product messaging.

• Manage the internal sales enablement tool and sales asset repository and act as primary administrator

• Support sales training and internal communications around new products, releases, positioning, and competitive insights.

• Provide timely support for sales requests related to product messaging, competitive information, and deal-specific needs.

 AI-Enabled Workflows

• Use AI tools to streamline research, competitive monitoring, content development, and other repetitive marketing workflows.

• Help test, improve, and maintain AI-assisted workflows while ensuring outputs remain accurate and aligned with business needs.

• Come up with new ways to use AI in the PMM lifecycle and build skills and agents to assist

 Competitive Intelligence & Win/Loss

• Monitor competitors, market trends, customer needs, and developments across the GRC landscape.

• Support the development and ongoing maintenance of competitive battlecards and sales resources for assigned products.

• Support win/loss analysis by organizing feedback and identifying trends.

 Requirements & Skills:

• 2-3 years of relevant experience in product marketing, B2B technology, SaaS, risk, compliance, or a related field.

• Experience working cross-functionally with Product, Sales, Marketing, or Customer teams.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to simplify complex products and concepts for different audiences.

• Experience creating marketing and sales enablement materials for B2B audiences.

• Comfortable conducting market and competitive research and turning findings into practical insights and assets.

• Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines.

• Comfortable working with marketing or business metrics and using data to inform decisions.

• Hands-on experience using AI tools to improve research, content creation, analysis, or marketing workflows.

• Experience in GRC, risk, compliance, cybersecurity, legal technology, or enterprise SaaS is an asset.

• Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, or a related field is an asset.

 What Success Looks Like Within the first 6–12 months, you will:

• Develop a strong understanding of Mitratech's GRC portfolio, customers, personas, and competitive landscape.

• Become a reliable partner to Product Management and Sales on product messaging and go-to-market execution for assigned products.

• Deliver high-quality positioning, launch, competitive, and sales enablement materials with increasing independence.

• Contribute meaningful competitive and win/loss insights that improve messaging and sales effectiveness.

• Identify opportunities to use AI and automation to make Product Marketing workflows more efficient.

• Build strong relationships across Marketing, Product, Sales, and Customer teams.

 This role can be performed 100% remote anywhere in the US. Given the need for team collaboration and meeting overlap, candidates who can align with Eastern Time Zone business hours are strongly preferred . Anticipated Pay Range: 70,000-80,000 USD Annually.

title: Finance Officer
description:
Vacancy for Finance Officer

Salary: Meridian Trust Support, Grade 7 Points 12-19

Hours of work: 37 hours / 42 weeks

Based at: Swavesey Village College, Gibraltar Lane, Swavesey, Cambs, CB24 4RS

We have an exciting opportunity for an enthusiastic and detail-oriented individual to join our expanding team as a Finance Officer. This role will assist the Trust Accountant in supporting, processing, and preparing accounting data for the training organisations within the Trust. This is a dynamic role with responsibility for a variety of tasks from monthly supplier payments and payroll administration to reconciliation of the balance sheet and plenty more between.

The Opportunity

  • A great chance to work with a strong, fun enthusiastic team.
  • To work within one of the most respected and admired Multi-Academy Trusts in the Country.
  • To develop new and existing skills within a finance role with access to development opportunities.
  • The ideal candidate
  • Experience working in an administrative or accounting environment.
  • Must have a full valid driving license and access to their own means of transport.
  • Have a working knowledge of accounts payable/receivable in conjunction with PSF or equivalent accounting software.
  • Possess the ability to manage own workload and meet deadlines effectively whilst maintaining high attention to detail.

Meridian Trust is a values-led organisation formed in 2011 that has risen to be one of the highest-performing academy trusts in the country. The Trust is founded on its commitment to a high-quality educational provision for all at the heart of local communities. Meridian currently operates primary, secondary and special schools across Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire, Peterborough, Lincolnshire and Northamptonshire.

Meridian Trust offers a wealth of fantastic benefits for teaching and support staff which are highlighted below but are not limited to -

  • Apprenticeship and CPD opportunities which allow you to gain specialist knowledge in a role you are passionate about developing in
  • Opportunity to jump start your career in teaching through our dedicated Initial Teacher Training Team (ITT)
  • Support for mental health and wellbeing through our Employee Assistance Programme and other resources
  • Cycle to work scheme
  • Defined benefit local government or Teacher’s pension scheme
  • Healthcare benefits including free eye test vouchers and flu vaccinations
  • Free on-site parking
  • Discounts on a wide range of benefits from everyday essentials to holidays

To explore our full range of benefits, please visit https://www.meridiantrust.co.uk/jobs-and-training/benefits/.

For more information about the role please download the Applicant Information Pack below.

Closing date for applications: 20 November 2026

Interviews will be held on: 3 December 2026

Meridian Trust reserves the right to close the applications early in the event that a suitable candidate is sourced.

The Trust is committed to diversity and inclusion and equality of opportunity for all staff and applications from individuals are encouraged regardless of age, disability, sex, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, race, religion or belief and marriage and civil partnerships.

The Trust is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. All appointments will be subject to pre-employment checks, including an enhanced check with the Disclosure & Barring Service (DBS), as well as online searches.

title: Head of Year (Non Teaching)
description:
Dear Candidate,

Thank you very much for your interest in becoming a Head of Year at Manchester Communication Academy. Manchester Communication Academy was first established in 2010 and has gone from strength to strength each academic year. The Academy has approximately 1300 students on roll in Years 7-11 and we boast a wonderfully rich and diverse school community. MCA is at the heart of the community and is committed to improving educational outcomes for all of our students. MCA is proud to be a community hub and our outward facing work is outstanding.

Our non-teaching Heads of Year lead the day-to-day pastoral care, conduct and standards of their year group. Working with the Teaching Director, Pastoral Programme Lead and specialist teams, they combine high expectations with practical support so that every pupil is known, valued and able to learn.

At MCA, we strive for excellence in everything we do. Implementing an ambitious, text-rich curriculum is a key priority and driving force in our ambition for excellence. We believe in the transformative power of knowledge in ensuring equitable opportunities for success. Our aspirational, bespoke curriculum ensures that all of our students gain the necessary experiences to compete academically, practically, socially and morally in the wider world. In order to achieve this, we invest deliberately in professional development. Drawing upon our EEF Research School, we are able to provide all staff with the most up-to-date and high quality evidence to develop their expertise.

At MCA, we proactively promote staff wellbeing through our management of workload and additional benefits for staff, such as flexi days and the Employee Assist programme. As a result, our staff are highly skilled and knowledgeable professionals who embrace new opportunities to learn more and keep getting better - a culture that permeates the academy amongst staff and students.

Our developments now focus on evolving the student experience and their sense of identity and belonging at MCA. We are continuing to develop student culture through a behaviour curriculum for staff and students where expectations and routines are explicitly taught and deliberately practised. Our students appreciate and relish the opportunity to learn and we support their effective learning behaviours through high expectations with emphasis on metacognition and our work with parents, families and the community. Having the highest expectations of our students means that our teachers can focus on teaching and our students can focus on learning. There needs to be relentless consistency with the implementation of the behaviour approach in every classroom, but this needs to be delivered with respect, to help drive the standards we are striving to achieve.

We are now looking for staff who are aligned with our values and will accelerate the school’s journey to excellence. The position is a great opportunity for someone who shares our passion for delivering educational excellence. The right candidate will be able to engage our young people and work effectively with our parents. You will work with authenticity, clarity and empathy and place the wellbeing of students at the core of all decisions.

If you are aligned to our mission and values, and could flourish with this opportunity, we very much look forward to hearing from you. We fully recommend that you take the opportunity to make an informal visit prior to making your application to see the school for yourself.

Kind Regards

Susan Watmough

Headteacher

title: Skills Planning Analyst
description:
Full Time | Permanent | £36,070 Per Annum

Who we are

Winner of the Best Place to Work at the Tech South West Awards 2025, City College Plymouth offers a culture the College is proud of. Our core values of Respect, Ownership and Integrity help create an environment that supports a passion for teaching and learning. These values guide our work as we enrich our community through knowledge, experience and skills so every student can achieve their best.

As one of the country’s largest providers of quality education and training, City College Plymouth is entering a period of transition to enable us to propel education into the future. We take pride in offering a learning environment and organisational culture that contribute positively to the health, wellbeing and sustainability of our community and enable all our students and staff to achieve their full potential.

The Role

To support the College's skills planning and curriculum development functions through the collection, modelling, analysis and reporting of labour market intelligence, student demand, employer requirements and performance data. The postholder will assist in informing skills and curriculum planning, supporting strategic decision-making and ensuring that the College's provision aligns with our strategic intent, as well as local, regional and national skills priorities.

The role will contribute to the development of curriculum plans that meet the needs of learners, employers and the wider economy.

What we're looking for

  • Experience of using Power BI or other business intelligence tools
  • Experience of using 4Cast or similar
  • Experience of producing reports and presenting information.
  • Strong understanding of data accuracy and confidentiality requirements.
  • Ability to interpret information and identify trends.

What will you bring to the role?

  • Analysing: Analysing new information and using it to inform strategic decisions and approaches.
  • Critical Thinking: Identifying trends and patterns, thinking ahead and making logical decisions
  • Interpreting: Interpreting quantitative data in various formats.
  • Delivering: Embracing challenges by trying out alternative approaches and strategies to deliver success

description:

  • Lead governance development initiatives to enhance governance effectiveness across Trustees, Committees and Local Governing Bodies.
  • Oversee governor and trustee recruitment, succession planning, engagement and diversity initiatives.
  • Develop and deliver governance training, induction programmes and development opportunities for governors, trustees and governance leaders.
  • Provide high-quality governance advice, guidance and strategic support to senior leaders, Trustees and governing bodies.

Key Requirements

  • Excellent stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence, advise and challenge constructively at senior level.

title: Student Support Coordinator
location: Leeds, Yorkshire and the Humber, GB
description:
About the Role

Leeds City College is recruiting a Student Support Coordinator to join our Visual Arts team based at Quarry Hill Campus. You will be working as part of a dedicated team to deliver a highly effective pastoral support service to students, helping them to overcome barriers to learning, achieve their potential, and progress successfully through their studies.

The Visual Arts department, based at the Quarry Hill Campus, is a vibrant and creative area offering courses in Art and Design, Fashion and Textiles, Photography, and Graphic Design. The department delivers programmes from Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 BTEC qualifications through to Access to Higher Education, providing learners with the skills, knowledge and experiences required for progression into higher education and careers within the creative industries.

Our students benefit from industry-standard studios, specialist workshops and creative learning environments that support the development of practical and professional skills. The department is committed to fostering creativity, inclusion and student success, ensuring that all learners are supported to achieve their individual goals.

What You Will Do

  • Work collaboratively with curriculum teams to support student success, attendance, retention and achievement by promoting wellbeing and helping to remove barriers to learning.

  • Provide high-quality pastoral support to learners across the department, particularly those who may be vulnerable or require additional support to engage successfully with their studies.

  • Deliver timely and effective short-term interventions, supporting students to develop strategies that enable them to remain engaged and make positive progress.

  • Signpost students to appropriate internal and external services, ensuring they receive the specialist support they need at the right time.

  • Act as a key safeguarding contact within the department, recording and reporting safeguarding concerns using appropriate systems and ensuring policies and procedures are followed.

  • Build positive and professional relationships with students, curriculum tutors, department leaders, support services and external agencies to ensure a coordinated approach to student support.

  • Promote a safe, inclusive and supportive learning environment where students feel valued, respected and able to succeed.

  • Undertake relevant training, including safeguarding, first aid and mental health awareness, in line with the requirements of the role.

About You

  • Level 2 Safeguarding qualification or willingness to achieve within one year of appointment.

  • Substantial relevant experience of supporting students who have additional support needs or who may be vulnerable.

  • English and Maths at Level 2.

  • Experience of working with young people in an educational or support setting.

  • Up-to-date knowledge and understanding of safeguarding, wellbeing and student support practices.

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build effective professional relationships with learners, curriculum staff, college support teams and external agencies.

  • Ability to work collaboratively with a range of stakeholders while maintaining professional boundaries and confidentiality.

  • A proactive, organised and student-centred approach, with a commitment to supporting positive learner outcomes.

description:
St Joseph’s College is an oversubscribed mixed Catholic grammar school with a long tradition of educational excellence. As part of the Laetare Catholic Multi-Academy Trust, we are proud of our strong ethos, high expectations and commitment to supporting the development of the whole person.

We are seeking an organised, approachable and accurate sixth form Secretary to provide day-to-day administrative support to our busy Sixth Form. The postholder will report to the Office Manager and work closely with the Senior Sixth Form Secretary.

What the role involves

Act as a welcoming first point of contact for sixth form students, parents, visitors and external contacts.

Maintain accurate student records, attendance and routine sixth form data, following agreed procedures for referral and escalation.

Provide administration for admissions, applications, induction and enrolment.

Support UCAS administration, student progression records and key deadlines.

Assist with communications, reports, events, trips, enrichment and examinations administration.

Experience of providing accurate administrative support and handling confidential information.

Excellent organisational, communication and IT skills, including confidence with email, word-processing and spreadsheets.

The ability to prioritise workload, remain professional during busy periods and work effectively with colleagues and young people.

A commitment to safeguarding and promoting students’ welfare. School, UCAS and MIS experience would be helpful but are not essential.

A supportive Catholic school community, friendly colleagues, professional development opportunities, a commitment to staff wellbeing, an Employee Assistance Programme, access to the relevant pension scheme, and good transport links with staff parking and EV charging points.

St Joseph’s College is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. We follow safer recruitment practices to ensure we appoint the right people to work with our students.

title: Director of Transformation
description:
The Mossbourne Federation seeks to appoint a Director of Transformation

Mossbourne Federation is the realisation of Sir Clive Borne’s dream to provide the children of Hackney with an outstanding education. Built on a formula of high expectations, doing the simple things right, and the belief that all children can succeed, Mossbourne offers an environment where all learners, regardless of ability, benefit from innovative and enlightened approaches to teaching and learning. Our calm working atmosphere creates well-rounded individuals who excel in the arts, on the sporting field, and academically.

Since the federation was formed in 2004, we are delighted to have expanded to include three Thurrock schools. We now consist of seven academies:

  • Mossbourne Community Academy (MCA) secondary and sixth form, Hackney

  • Mossbourne Fobbing Academy (MFA) secondary and sixth form, Thurrock

  • Mossbourne Herd Lane Academy (MHLA) primary, Thurrock

  • Mossbourne Parkside Academy (MPA) primary, Hackney

  • Mossbourne Port Side Academy (MPSA) secondary, Thurrock

  • Mossbourne Riverside Academy (MRA) primary, Hackney

  • Mossbourne Victoria Park Academy (MVPA) secondary, Hackney

The role will provide short-term transformation capacity to assess, design, implement and embed a single, evidence-led system of executive educational assurance and accountability, centred on Team Around an Academy (TAA). The ultimate purpose is to ensure every Mossbournian thrives through exceptional educational provision, with outstanding pupil outcomes at the heart of all activity.

The postholder will establish clear executive responsibilities, reliable data, standardised reporting and verifiable follow-through, and contribute to testing and embedding a revised Scheme of Delegation. The work must align with the Academy Trust Handbook 2026, the DfE Academy Trust Governance Guide and Mossbourne’s governing documents. The Federation’s Head of Governance retains responsibility for independent governance advice, the formal governance framework and board approval processes and the Executive Principal, Education Operations remains focused on delivery of other operational improvement programmes to support the Federation’s strategy.

Working for a Mossbourne Federation Academy means being part of a community of exceptional practitioners. Colleagues are warm, welcoming, and supportive of each other. As one of the country’s leading federations, staff expectations are high. The Mossbourne Federation engages with, and supports its workforce, thus creating an inspirational working environment which nurtures the development of personal and professional excellence.

Federation staff are rewarded through the comprehensive package of benefits listed in our Federation Recruitment Brochure, including:

Private healthcare, to support health and wellbeing, fully paid by the Federation

Early finish on Friday - secondary academies

Hybrid working for planning and preparation time - primary academies

The Mossbourne Allowance*

Free lunches*

Free staff fitness classes and/or use of onsite gym - secondary academies

Cycle to work and season ticket loan schemes

Discounts at local restaurants

Discounted gym membership with the ability to spread membership costs

Saturday and holiday paid programme

Special leave scheme (additional paid time off)

Staff appreciation awards and events

First rate professional development and career opportunities

Financial support for career development*

‘Introduction Bonus’ for current staff*

Remuneration for exam board marking*

Tea, coffee and refreshments provided for staff throughout the week

*Terms and conditions apply for some benefits

If you are passionate about innovative education, have a commitment to personal excellence and are ready for a new challenge, we welcome your application.

Please note that CVs or incomplete application forms will not be considered. All other applications will be considered; however, only shortlisted applicants will be contacted. Mossbourne Federation reserves the right to close adverts earlier than the stated deadline.

At Mossbourne Federation, we know diversity fosters creativity and innovation. We are committed to equality of opportunity, to being fair and inclusive, and to being a place where all belong. We do not discriminate in recruitment or during employment based on any protected characteristic or aspect of individual identity. We are committed to anti-racist principles and practices, and we welcome individuals with the ethos and energy to help us achieve this goal.

The Mossbourne Federation is committed to safeguarding the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff to share this commitment. Applicants will be required to undergo child protection screening appropriate to the post, including checks with past employers and the Disclosure and Barring Service.

You can follow us on LinkedIn at - https://www.linkedin.com/company/mossbourne-federation/

Find more about working with Mossbourne Federation in our Federation Recruitment and Employee Experience Brochures.

location: Leeds, Yorkshire and the Humber, GB
description:
About the Role

Leeds City College are recruiting for a Data & Performance Officer in the Quality of Education team.

In this role, you will manage the full data lifecycle, from initial collection and preparation through to analysis and interpretation. You will develop and maintain dashboards, monitor key trends, and communicate meaningful, actionable insights to stakeholders, ensuring the highest standards of data accuracy, governance, and GDPR compliance.

You will also serve as the primary point of contact for data-related enquiries, provide tailored systems training to enhance staff knowledge and confidence, and undertake essential administrative responsibilities to support the smooth running of the department.

If you do not already hold a Level 4 or higher data qualification, you will complete a Level 4 Data Analysis Apprenticeship as part of the role.

Please note that this vacancy may close earlier than advertised, so we recommend submitting your application as soon as possible to avoid missing out.

What You Will Do

  • Work with stakeholders to understand their information needs and define appropriate reporting requirements.

  • Source, extract, organise, cleanse, and analyse data from multiple systems, ensuring high levels of consistency, accuracy, and quality.

  • Design, develop, and maintain reports and interactive dashboards to track performance, highlight potential risks, and identify areas for improvement and opportunity.

  • Examine datasets to identify trends, patterns, and emerging insights that support informed decision-making.

  • Interpret and communicate analytical findings to colleagues and stakeholders, presenting complex information in a easy to understand format to aid evidence-based decisions.

  • Handle sensitive and confidential information with the utmost integrity, conducting regular data quality checks and ensuring full compliance with GDPR and relevant data protection standards.

  • Participate in the evaluation and review of data projects, identifying key learnings and opportunities to improve future processes and initiatives.

About You

  • Level 2 qualifications in English and Maths (Grade A–C or equivalent), alongside a relevant Level 3 or Level 4 qualification applicable to the role.

  • Practical experience using business or education software, including intermediate/advanced Excel (formulas and pivot tables), Google Workspace and management information systems such as ProSolution, ProAchieve or OneFile, with the ability to analyse data, identify trends and recommend improvements.

  • Proven ability to build effective, working relationships with colleagues and stakeholders at all levels.

  • Strong IT, numerical and data management skills, with excellent attention to detail, a professional and confidential approach to handling information, and the ability to communicate complex data clearly to a range of audiences.

  • Excellent interpersonal, problem-solving and communication skills, with the ability to use initiative and a proactive, solution-focused approach to enhance service delivery.

title: Trust Lead for Computing and Digital Learning
description:
Passionate about computing education? Want to inspire pupils of all ages through STEM?

Committed to transforming lives through education?

Do you have deep expertise in computing education, digital learning curriculum design and

pedagogy, and a proven track record of securing strong outcomes for young people?

CAM Academy Trust is seeking a Trust Lead for Computing and Digital Learning to shape and

deliver our vision for digital excellence across our family of schools. This is a rare opportunity to

lead the development of our Trust-wide digital learning strategy, ensuring that technology

enhances teaching, learning and outcomes for every pupil.

We are looking for a highly credible practitioner and leader who combines subject expertise with

strategic thinking. You will champion high-quality computing education and digital learning,

support schools to develop innovative and evidence-informed digital pedagogy, and drive

improvement through collaboration, professional learning and curriculum excellence. You will

be knowledgeable, and able to advise and support decision-making around when ed-tech may

enhance learning and also when it may not.

A key priority for the role will be to rapidly, but sustainably, raise standards in computing across

our schools. You will work collaboratively, with computing leaders and teachers across our

schools to develop a thriving subject community. You will lead in a way that will secure

sustainable excellence. You will be particularly driven by improving outcomes for our most

vulnerable and disadvantaged young people.

As a key member of our wider school improvement team, you will also lead the development of

our approach to artificial intelligence, shaping both our AI strategy and the professional learning

that will equip staff to use AI confidently, responsibly and effectively.

At CAM, we are making an absolute commitment to placing STEM at the heart of our pupil

entitlement as part of a strong place-based offer, given our schools are in the regional orbit of

Cambridge. We are seeking someone who is excited by this ambition and ready to build the

local and regional partnerships, industry links and opportunities that will inspire young people

and prepare them for the future. You will play a leading role in ensuring our STEM offer is

innovative, relevant and cutting edge.

As a Trust we are committed to the concept of all-through education. Our primaries feed into

our secondaries. There is an exciting opportunity here to work collaboratively on an all-through

digital strategy. We are keen to hear from candidates who have some experience in both primary

and secondary, even if their experience is predominantly in one or the other.

The post-holder will teach. Teaching is at the heart of what we do and holding a teaching

commitment supports that important principle. There is flexibility around the teaching

commitment, which will not be full time, and this can be discussed and agreed with the

successful candidate.

If you are a credible, smart and forward-thinking leader who wants to make a system-wide

impact across a thriving and ambitious trust, we would love to hear from you.

Join us and help shape the future of computing, digital learning, AI and STEM for thousands

of young people.

title: Speech & Language Therapists (All Levels) in Bucks
description:
Chiltern Way Academy Trust is a highly successful, award‑winning Specialist Multi Academy Trust with multiple state‑of‑the‑art campuses. Our teams work across a broad range of Autism Spectrum Condition (ASC) and Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) needs, delivering innovative, transformational education and exceptional care that changes the life chances of young people every day.

Across our nine sites, we offer outstanding facilities and a highly skilled staff team, enabling us to deliver exceptional education and care across the full range of behavioural and communication needs.

The Opportunity

We are expanding our multidisciplinary therapy provision and are seeking Speech & Language Therapists at all levels to join our teams across Bucks , including an exciting Senior Speech & Language Therapist leadership opportunity.

These roles offer the chance to contribute to a developing, forward-thinking service where communication is at the heart of learning and inclusion.

About the RolesSpeech & Language Therapist / Specialist Speech & Language Therapist

You will play a key role in establishing and developing speech and language therapy provision across the Trust.

You will:

  • Deliver specialist, outcome-focused interventions for pupils with a wide range of speech, language and communication needs (SLCN)
  • Embed communication strategies across the curriculum to support access to learning
  • Work collaboratively with staff, families, and external professionals to ensure a holistic approach
  • Contribute to staff training and professional development, supporting a whole-school approach to SLCN
Senior Speech & Language Therapist

In this key leadership role, you will:

  • Lead the development and delivery of a specialist speech and language therapy service for pupils with highly complex needs
  • Provide advanced clinical expertise and oversee therapy provision across your site
  • Embed communication strategies across the curriculum at a strategic level
  • Deliver and oversee training, supervision, and staff development
  • Coordinate multidisciplinary working and contribute to service development and quality assurance
  • Provide clinical leadership within your area of responsibility
About You

We are looking for passionate professionals who bring:

  • A recognised qualification in Speech & Language Therapy with HCPC and RCSLT registration
  • Experience working with children and young people with ASC, SEMH, and complex communication needs
  • Strong communication, organisational, and collaborative working skills

For senior roles, you will also demonstrate:

  • Significant clinical experience
  • Strong leadership and clinical decision-making skills
  • A passion for developing others and driving high-quality, outcome-focused practice
Why Join Us?
  • Be part of a highly respected, award-winning Trust
  • Work in state-of-the-art environments with a supportive multidisciplinary team
  • Play a key role in shaping and developing therapy services
  • Make a genuine and lasting difference to young people’s lives

Join us—and help transform communication, unlock potential, and change futures.

Our Commitment

Equality, Diversity and Inclusion are at the heart of everything we do. We are committed to creating a culture where everyone feels valued and supported to thrive.

Chiltern Way Academy Trust is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. All staff are expected to share this commitment. The successful candidates will be required to undergo an enhanced DBS check.

The Trust complies with its obligations under GDPR and data protection legislation.

title: Residential Accommodation Services Manager
description:
Residential Accommodation Services Manager

Wiltshire College & University Centre – Lackham Campus

Be part of something special. Create a place where students feel at home, build confidence and thrive.

Wiltshire College & University Centre is looking for an enthusiastic, experienced and student-focused Residential Accommodation Services Manager to lead our residential provision at Lackham Campus.

This is an excellent opportunity to take the lead in creating an outstanding residential experience for students, ensuring that those living away from home feel safe, supported, included and part of a vibrant college community. You'll be at the heart of campus life, making a real difference to students' wellbeing, independence, personal development and success.

Set within 500 acres of beautiful Wiltshire countryside, Lackham Campus offers a truly unique learning environment. With a commercial farm, Agri-Tech Centre, Animal Centre, engineering workshops and dedicated horticulture areas, our campus is a thriving, practical and industry-focused environment where learners work with real-world land-based systems and emerging technologies.

As Residential Accommodation Services Manager, you'll have the opportunity to shape the residential experience, lead a dedicated team and work alongside colleagues across the college to create a safe, welcoming and supportive home-from-home environment. You'll also play a vital role in ensuring our provision for under-18s meets the relevant Care Standards and the highest expectations of safeguarding and student welfare.

🌟 What We Offer

💷 Salary: £36,955 per year⏱️ Contract Type: Permanent, Full-Time 37 hours per week, 52 weeks per year📍 Campus: Lackham Campus


A fantastic opportunity to combine leadership, student wellbeing and operational management in a unique college environment where no two days are the same.

What You'll Do

  • Lead and inspire the residential team, creating a positive, professional and student-focused service.
  • Oversee the day-to-day management of residential accommodation, ensuring high standards across all aspects of provision.
  • Create a welcoming and inclusive residential community where students feel safe, valued and supported.
  • Understand and ensure residential services for under-18s meet the relevant Care Standards, maintaining appropriate policies, procedures and quality assurance arrangements.
  • Take responsibility for student welfare, safeguarding and pastoral care, ensuring concerns are identified and managed effectively.
  • Develop opportunities for residential activities and enrichment that encourage friendships, independence and personal development.
  • Work closely with curriculum, safeguarding and student support teams to provide joined-up support.
  • Build positive relationships with parents, carers, external agencies and other partners.
  • Oversee residential admissions, room allocations, arrivals and departures.
  • Ensure accommodation meets required standards for health and safety, security, cleanliness and maintenance.
  • Manage staffing, budgets and resources effectively, ensuring an efficient and high-quality service.
  • Maintain accurate records and ensure compliance with college policies and regulatory requirements.
  • Lead, motivate and develop the residential team, driving high standards and continuous improvement.

What You'll Bring

  • Experience managing residential accommodation, student services, pastoral support or a similar service.
  • Proven experience of leading, motivating and developing a team.
  • A strong understanding of safeguarding, student welfare and pastoral care, particularly for under-18s.
  • Knowledge of the Care Standards and regulatory requirements relating to residential provision for young people.
  • Experience of health and safety, risk management and maintaining safe environments.
  • The confidence to manage challenging situations, make sound decisions and resolve issues effectively.
  • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Experience managing budgets, staffing and operational resources.
  • A positive, proactive and solutions-focused approach.
  • A genuine passion for supporting young people to develop independence, confidence and life skills.
  • The ability to inspire a team and create a culture where high standards, care and accountability go hand in hand.

✨ Why Choose This Path?

This is more than an accommodation management role. It's an opportunity to shape an important part of student life and make a lasting difference to young people.

Join us and enjoy the opportunity to:

  • Lead and develop a residential service that plays a vital role in the student experience.
  • Make a meaningful difference to young people's confidence, independence and wellbeing.
  • Build a positive residential community where students feel they belong.
  • Work alongside passionate colleagues in a unique 500-acre specialist campus environment.
  • Influence the quality, development and future direction of residential provision.
  • Make a visible difference every day, knowing that the environment you create helps students succeed.

⚡ Make a Move That Truly Matters

If you're a passionate residential or student support professional with the leadership skills, energy and enthusiasm to make a difference, we'd love to hear from you.

This is your opportunity to bring people together, inspire a team and create a residential experience that students will remember for all the right reasons.

🚀 Help us make Lackham more than a place to study. Make it a place where students feel at home, discover their potential and thrive.

                                                                          This is a key senior operational leadership role, offering the opportunity to shape the strategic direction of our estate while ensuring our schools remain safe, secure, compliant and inspiring environments for pupils and staff.

title: Backend Software Engineer - Data Connectors
description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.
 
The Role
 
The Connectivity team builds the software that connects Palantir’s platform to customer systems. Our connectors integrate databases, enterprise applications, cloud storage, web services, and streaming systems, enabling customers to bring data into Foundry and write back to their operational systems. From large datasets to real-time events and user-driven interactions, these connections underpin the applications and AI workflows customers build with Foundry and AIP.
 
You’ll build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connector suite and the shared infrastructure behind it. You’ll work across the stack, taking ownership of connector implementations, developer SDKs, and the systems that build, test, distribute, and run our connectivity software.
 
A central part of this work is evolving and scaling a large, established codebase. You’ll move integrations from bespoke infrastructure onto shared platform capabilities, design SDKs that enable other teams and customers to build integrations independently, and safely retire older implementations. You’ll also build observability and diagnostic tools that help users understand, monitor, and troubleshoot their connections. You’ll own improvements from design through production and use what you learn from operating connectors to strengthen the platform they share.

title: Salesforce Business Systems Administrator
description:
Headquarters: United States, Remote

 ROLE: Business Systems Administrator

 Location: United States, Remote

 This is a fully remote opportunity and can be worked from any location in the United States.

 ABOUT THE COMPANY:

 Salesloft is building the next era of enterprise revenue — one where teams make confident decisions powered by AI and real signals. By combining our scale, insights, and AI innovation, we're building the industry's first Predictive Revenue System, enabling humans and AI to work together to make smarter decisions and drive consistent growth.

 With thousands of customers using our platforms every day, we have an unmatched view into how revenue is actually won — the Revenue Context that reveals what happens, when, and with what outcome. This gives us a unique opportunity to transform an entire category and set a new benchmark for how modern revenue teams operate.

 Join us to help transform how companies around the world run revenue — and build the platform that will guide leading revenue teams into the future.

 THE OPPORTUNITY

 At Salesloft, our Business Systems Administrator, Customer Experience is critical to our company’s success. You will be a key member of our fast-growing and high-performing Business Systems team and will lead generating, scoping, solutioning, and executing process and efficiency improvement efforts across customer-focused systems. You will have a passionate, capable team supporting you.

 You will be responsible for the support, development, and maintenance of Salesforce and its related Customer Experience systems. You must own the pursuit of a world-class technology experience for our customers, while enabling scale and efficiency for internal customer experience teams - Support, Services, and Success. You need to have pride in the work you do and a passion for customer support and success.

 On a day to day basis, you will:

• Work with Services, Success, and Support teams to identify manual process that can be automated

• Scope, Plan, Recommend, and Deliver system solutions that help these teams meet their Objectives and Key Results

• Play a leading role in the exploration, design, build, delivery, and support of a redesigned and improved Customer Hub

 This role lives at the heart of how we Make Your Mark: you'll treat systems administration as a discipline — automating, documenting, and fixing root causes so the same issues don't recur. And in the spirit of how we are Customer Inspired — where every decision has a true north, and it's our customer — you'll administer access and configuration as the security controls they are, protecting the company and the data customers trust us with.

 WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 We are seeking a Salesforce CRM, and related customer experience systems, expert. Someone that can see the big picture, future state but has a keen eye for details. You will have a knack for spotting opportunities to improve systems and process, and are excited to work cross-functionally to make it happen. You are passionate to build relationships to help others succeed.

 If you’re looking for an opportunity to learn more, do more, and become more, then becoming a Business Systems Administrator is the career path for you!

 THE TEAM

 Our Salesloft’s Revenue Operations team is comprised of seasoned and up-and-coming operational experts.

 Values: Move as One, Evidence over Ego, Lead from the Front, Make Your Mark, Customer-Inspired.

 The Revenue Operations team consists of team members that work with Sales, Marketing, Customer Services, Finance, and IT to create systems to more efficiently prospect, forecast, close, onboard, and support customers. Team members conceptualize the strategic priorities for the company, develop execution plans, execute plans cross-functionally, and operationalize executed strategies for continuous improvement.

 THE SKILL SET

• Bachelor's degree

• 3+ years experience in a related role, Software (SaaS) experience is a plus

• 2-3 years experience administering Salesforce Service Cloud, Salesforce Knowledge, Live Agent, and Customer Communities preferred

• Salesforce Administrator certification is required

• Salesforce Service Cloud Consultant certification is a plus

• Demonstrated experience designing, revising and managing Salesforce Flows

• Ability to lead teams through change management and business transformations

• Excellent project management skills and the ability to collaborate with management and others in the company

• Disciplined, flexible, and autonomous work habits; we don't micromanage

• Understanding of the SaaS business model and culture is a plus

 At Salesloft, we are committed to creating an inclusive and supportive workplace where everyone belongs and can thrive. We focus on culture add, not culture fit, and believe our teams are made stronger by the unique perspectives, experiences, and identities each person brings.

 We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and provide employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, or any other characteristic protected by law.

 If you're excited about this role even though your experience may not perfectly match every requirement, we encourage you to apply. We are actively hiring across multiple geographies and would love to welcome passionate, curious, and mission-driven individuals to our growing team. Explore our open roles and consider joining us!

 Please note that all official communication regarding job opportunities at Salesloft will come from an @salesloft.com email address. If you receive messages on LinkedIn or other job platforms claiming to be from Salesloft, they may not be legitimate. To verify the authenticity of any job-related communication, please visit our official Careers Page ( https://salesloft.com/company/careers/ ).

 We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, notetaking, or summarizing responses. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment — all hiring decisions are made by people. If you would like more information about how your data is processed or prefer to opt out of any AI-assisted tools, please let your recruiter know. Opting out will not impact your experience or consideration.

title: DevOps Engineer, Edge and Developer Experience (Remote Eligible in Bulgaria)
description:
Headquarters: -REMOTE, BULGARIA-

 For over 20 years, Smartsheet has empowered teams to manage work seamlessly and scale solutions smarter. Now, in our most ambitious chapter yet, we are uniting human teams with AI agents. By orchestrating the work agents do best, automating manual tasks and uncovering insights at scale, we create the space for people to focus on what truly matters: judgment, creativity, and big thinking. That is magic at work, and it’s what we show up for every day.

 We are seeking a DevOps Engineer II to join the Edge and Developer Experience team. Our team collaboratively operates Smartsheet's high-performance edge proxy platform and drives the adoption of internal engineering tooling. The edge proxy serves as the entry point for all traffic across Smartsheet's commercial and FedRAMP-authorized US Government environments. The team supports the lifecycle of this platform: from maintaining proxy configurations, to provisioning the multi-region AWS EKS infrastructure it runs on, to assisting with observability. Beyond the edge layer, the team also drives the integration of internal developer tooling — from а developer portal (IDP) to standardized CI/CD pipelines — that improves the engineering experience and velocity across the company.

 You will work remotely from Bulgaria and report to one of our engineering leaders in Bulgaria.

 You will:

• Contribute to the edge proxy platform: Assist in maintaining, upgrading, and extending a high-performance reverse proxy. This includes writing Go and Python automation, managing container images on hardened Linux bases, and working with CDN and traffic management capabilities.

• Build and maintain cloud infrastructure as code: Implement Terraform/Terragrunt modules and live environment configurations for EKS clusters, load balancers, IAM roles, and supporting AWS services.

• Operate Kubernetes clusters: Assist in managing multi-region EKS deployments via GitOps workflows (e.g., FluxCD, ArgoCD) and Helm charts.

• Support CI/CD pipelines: Help design, maintain, and improve shared GitLab CI/CD pipeline templates used across team repositories, embedding DevSecOps guardrails.

• Automate operational toil: Build tooling for tasks such as container image patching, EKS AMI rotation, and automated patching cycles.

• Manage observability: Help provision and maintain Datadog SLOs, monitors, and dashboards; participate in the team's on-call rotation responding to incidents.

• Support Developer Experience initiatives: Assist in the rollout and integration of various platforms to reduce cognitive load for engineering teams.

• Apply AI tools: Leverage AI-based workflows within your domain to improve project execution, infrastructure design, and debugging.

 You Have:

• 2–4 years of experience in DevOps, Platform Engineering, or Site Reliability Engineering.

• A BS or MS in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent industry experience.

• Hands-on experience with Terraform for managing cloud infrastructure.

• Experience with Kubernetes operations and AWS services (EKS, VPC, IAM, ECR).

• Proficiency in at least one general-purpose programming language — Go or Python preferred — for building operational automation.

• Experience designing or maintaining CI/CD pipelines (GitLab CI/CD preferred).

• Familiarity with container image security practices and GitOps workflows.

• A strong operational mindset with a willingness to participate in on-call rotations and incident response.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Fluency in English is required.

• Familiarity with leveraging AI-based workflows to author or maintain code/infrastructure.

• Legally eligible to work in Bulgaria on an ongoing basis.

 Nice to Have:

• Understanding of reverse proxies, API gateways, or load balancers (NGINX, HAProxy, or equivalent).

• Familiarity with FedRAMP or AWS GovCloud operational constraints.

• Experience managing Datadog resources via infrastructure as code.

• Experience integrating internal developer portals or feature flag management tools.

title: Senior AI Engineer - EU
description:
Headquarters: Germany (Remote) ; Ireland (Remote); Netherlands (Remote) ; Portugal (Remote) ; Spain (Remote) ; United Kingdom (Remote)

 Who we are

 Typeform is a refreshingly different form builder. We help over 150,000 businesses collect the data they need with forms, surveys, and quizzes that people enjoy. Designed to look striking and feel effortless to fill out, Typeform drives 500 million responses every year—and integrates with essential tools like Slack, Zapier, and Hubspot.

 Typeform is fully remote by design. For this role, we can hire candidates based in the UK, Ireland, Germany, Portugal, Spain or The Netherlands

 About the team

 The AI Engineering team builds the systems and capabilities behind Typeform’s AI products, including Research Flow, our platform for combining quantitative research with deeper qualitative insights.

 We use machine learning, large language models, RAG, and agentic systems to help customers collect, understand, and act on information in more conversational and personalised ways.

 Through Research Flow, this includes helping customers design studies, run AI-moderated conversations with adaptive follow-up questions, and turn responses into useful insights.

 The team owns the journey from experimentation through to production. This includes AI application development, evaluation, infrastructure, deployment, observability, reliability, and performance.

 You will work closely with Product Managers, Software Engineers, Data Scientists, Data Engineers, and Analytics teams to turn promising AI ideas into secure, scalable, and dependable customer experiences.

 About the role

 As a Senior AI Engineer at Typeform, you will be instrumental in building and evolving the AI capabilities behind Research Flow, alongside our broader AI products.

 Your work will help customers understand the “why” behind responses and move from research questions to informed decisions faster.

 Your scope will span generative AI applications, enterprise RAG systems, agentic workflows, model evaluation, machine learning pipelines, and the infrastructure required to run them reliably at scale.

 This is a hands-on engineering role with strong ownership. You will turn ideas and prototypes into production systems used by our customers, with direct influence on their quality and performance. You will also help define the technical standards for developing, evaluating, deploying, and monitoring AI across Typeform.

 Things you will do

 Build and deliver AI products

• Design, build, and deploy generative AI capabilities across Typeform’s products, with a key contribution to Research Flow.

• Develop applications using large language models, RAG, vector search, and agentic systems.

• Build services and APIs that allow product teams to integrate AI capabilities into customer experiences.

• Turn prototypes into reliable production systems with clear measures of performance and quality.

• Explore new ways for customers to collect, understand, and act on information using AI.

 Build scalable AI systems

• Design and operate machine learning services and workflows using Python, Docker, Kubernetes, and AWS.

• Build reliable pipelines for batch and real time processing using technologies such as Kafka and Airflow.

• Design solutions using vector databases to support retrieval, recommendations, personalisation, and semantic search.

• Use MLflow to manage experiments, model versions, registries, and deployments.

• Improve the reliability, performance, scalability, and cost efficiency of our AI systems.

 Evaluate and improve AI quality

• Build automated evaluation pipelines for generative AI applications, including the conversational and analytical capabilities behind Research Flow.

• Develop benchmarks that measure accuracy, relevance, reliability, fairness, latency, and cost.

• Evaluate retrieval strategies, including chunking, embeddings, context selection, and reranking.

• Monitor AI systems in production and identify opportunities to improve their quality and performance.

• Create safeguards that reduce unexpected behaviour and protect customer data.

 Shape our AI engineering practice

• Establish reusable patterns and technical standards for building, evaluating, and releasing AI systems.

• Help teams make informed decisions about models, frameworks, infrastructure, performance, and cost.

• Apply strong engineering practices across testing, security, observability, version control, and deployment.

• Share technical knowledge and support the development of other engineers.

• Keep up with relevant AI research, tools, and engineering practices, applying what is useful to Typeform.

 Collaborate across Typeform

• Partner with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Data Engineering, and Analytics teams to connect AI investments with customer and business needs.

• Work with Data Scientists to turn experiments and models into reliable production services.

• Communicate technical concepts, risks, and tradeoffs clearly to technical and nontechnical partners.

• Contribute to technical planning and help shape the direction of AI across Typeform.

 What you bring

• At least four years of experience building and deploying machine learning or AI systems in production.

• Strong Python and software engineering skills.

• Experience building production services using Python frameworks such as FastAPI.

• Practical experience developing generative AI applications using large language models, RAG, tool use, or agentic systems.

• Experience with frameworks such as PyTorch, LangChain, LangGraph, or similar technologies.

• A strong understanding of enterprise RAG systems, including chunking, embeddings, retrieval, reranking, evaluation, and monitoring.

• Experience creating automated evaluations for generative AI applications.

• Experience with AWS, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, and continuous integration and deployment practices.

• Experience using services such as AWS SageMaker or AWS Bedrock.

• Experience with Kafka, vector databases, or other technologies used for real time and high dimensional data processing.

• Experience managing machine learning workflows using MLflow.

• Experience monitoring production systems with tools such as Datadog or OpenSearch.

• The ability to balance quality, speed, reliability, scalability, and cost when making technical decisions.

• Strong communication skills and experience collaborating with Product, Engineering, and Data teams.

 Extra awesome

• Experience working in a B2B SaaS product company.

• Experience with orchestration tools such as Airflow or Argo Workflows.

• Familiarity with SQL, Spark, Snowflake, or other data processing technologies.

• Experience building systems that combine structured data, unstructured data, and generative AI.

• Experience with AI security, privacy, responsible AI, prompt injection protection, or data leakage prevention.

• Experience improving the latency and cost of AI systems operating at scale.

 *Typeform drives hundreds of millions of interactions each year, enabling conversational, human-centered experiences across the globe. We move as one team , empowering our collective efforts by valuing each individual’s unique perspective. This fosters strong bonds grounded in respect, transparency, and trust. We champion our diverse customer base by anticipating their needs and addressing their challenges with priority. Committed to excellence, we hold high expectations for ourselves and each other, continuously striving to deliver exceptional results.

 We are proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and stand firmly against discrimination and harassment of any kind—whether based on race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or expression, or veteran status. Everyone is welcome here.
